caption:
OpenAI announced on Sept 8, 2026 a multi-agent proof addressing forced versions of Navier-Stokes (about 10,000 agents, 88 hours, Lean formalisation in 17 hours) and says it will not claim the prize. On Sept 11, 25 Fields Medalists called AI-benchmark maths a 'severe misalignment'. Not peer-reviewed. Coverage: Nature news, Quanta, 2026.

#ai #mathematics #science #openai
voiceover_script: An AI, quote, solved, unquote, a million dollar maths problem. That is the headline. Here is the contested version. On September eighth, OpenAI announced that a system of around ten thousand agents, running for about eighty eight hours, produced a proof addressing forced versions of the Navier-Stokes equations, with a further seventeen hours to formalise it in Lean. Forced versus unforced matters here, and OpenAI itself says it will not claim the prize. Three days later, twenty five Fields Medalists published a statement calling AI benchmark mathematics a severe misalignment. The work is not peer-reviewed, and a priority dispute has been reported. Big claim, big pushback. We will follow it. Sources in the caption.
